result.title: Multimodal Models Can See, But Can They Think? A Study of Turkish Visual Reasoning
result.summary: Vision-Language Models have had massive leaps in recent years. Yet, when tested on high-level cognitive tasks like pattern completion, abstract logic, and relational reasoning, they still fall short. This limitation stems from the models' lack of ability to find out underlying rules and maintain constant intermediate steps, rather than merely deciding on the correct option. To research these shortcomings, this study analyzes visual reasoning performance throughout a multilingual evaluation framework encompassing the BİLSEM, MM-IQ, Visual Puzzles, and PuzzleVQA datasets. We evaluate various data mixing strategies and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) methods. We observed that a correct answer does not always mean the reasoning chain is valid. Because of this, we adopt an LLM-as-a-Judge approach to assess the quality of reasoning beyond final answer accuracy. Our experimental results reveal that baseline models often exhibit more stable reasoning compared to fine-tuned counterparts. Most importantly, we observe that SFT can lead to model collapse, manifesting as infinite text loops or empty outputs. The study concludes that current VLMs still struggle with abstract visual reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在多语言框架下评测视觉语言模型的抽象视觉推理，涵盖 BİLSEM、MM-IQ、Visual Puzzles 与 PuzzleVQA，比较多种数据混合与 SFT 策略，并用 LLM-as-a-Judge 在最终答案之外评估推理链质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 属 VLM 抽象视觉推理的诊断与失败分析：报告「答案正确不等于推理链有效」、微调后推理稳定性下降乃至文本循环或空输出式崩塌，可作为核查训练监督与推理链评价对 latent 推理影响的线索；但未涉及内部状态或视觉证据读取机制。
